Trump Wants to Kick ‘Rogue Activist Judges’ Off Cases. Can He?
item.description: “It’s a war, man,” Todd Blanche said a year ago at a convention of conservative lawyers. Blanche, then the Justice Department’s second-in-command and now the attorney general, was talking about the administration’s attitude toward the “rogue activist judges” who stood in its way. The battles have only gotten fiercer. In recent weeks alone, the Trump administration has filed three recusal motions and a misconduct complaint aimed at a total of eight judges in Washington and Minnesota. So can the administration force disfavored judges off its cases? Let’s take a look at what court decisions and ethics opinions have to say. One motion sought to disqualify Judge Ana Reyes for her handling of a case in which she temporarily blocked President Trump’s plan to create a fancy golf course in a Washington park. The Justice Department said she should step away from the dispute because, among other things, she had repeatedly raised her voice while addressing the administration’s lawyers, “blending aggression with systematic disrespect for a coequal branch of government.” Trump, not exactly modeling the behavior his lawyers sought from Judge Reyes, then proceeded to call her “a crazed lunatic” who “may be insane.” Judge Reyes, who was appointed by President Joe Biden, denied the motion two days after it was filed. In a 13-page opinion, she said she had not barred the government from taking any actions in the park for the better part of a year, asking only to be notified of changes. She said she had not expected to be told at 4:55 p.m. on the Friday of a holiday weekend that workers would the next morning begin removing what would turn out to be about 400 trees. That left her “furious” and “beyond disappointed,” she wrote, and she had said as much. “It is easy to weaponize selective quotations to bring a baseless recusal motion,” she wrote. “But it is much harder to meet the demanding legal standard against a full record.” The leading Supreme Court opinion in this area, Liteky v. United States in 1994, made a point that anyone who has spent time in a courtroom knows. Judge sometimes lose their tempers and yell. “Expressions of impatience, dissatisfaction, annoyance and even anger” are “within the bounds of what imperfect men and women, even after having been confirmed as federal judges, sometimes display,” Justice Antonin Scalia wrote for the majority. “A judge’s ordinary efforts at courtroom administration — even a stern and short-tempered judge’s ordinary efforts at courtroom administration — remain immune.” On the other side of the line, wrote Justice Scalia, who died in 2016, is “such a high degree of favoritism or antagonism as to make fair judgment impossible.” He added that not all bias is unwarranted. “One would not say, for example,” he wrote, “that world opinion is biased or prejudiced against Adolf Hitler.” The Justice Department also filed a misconduct complaint and two recusal motions aimed at federal judges in Minnesota who spoke to The New York Times about the immigration enforcement surge there last winter. Judge Patrick Schiltz, for instance, said that the Justice Department had been overwhelmed by litigation following the surge, leading to “a grave threat to the rule of law.” The complaint said Judge Schiltz, who was appointed by President George W. Bush, had delivered “unethical and partisan commentary concerning matters that are still indisputably pending.” The ethical standards are different for statements judges make outside court. They may not, ethics rules say, comment on the merits of pending cases, make inappropriately partisan statements or otherwise undermine public confidence in their impartiality. But judges are allowed to address judicial independence and security and to speak out to defend the rule of law. In a letter on Monday responding to the Justice Department’s complaint, 174 former judges said the statements the Minnesota judges had made to The Times were proper. “A court that cannot secure compliance with its orders cannot perform its constitutional function,” the letter said, “and a judge who explains that fact is addressing the administration of justice in the most basic sense.” In response to the complaint, Rebeccah Parks, a spokeswoman for the Federal District Court in Minnesota, said “our judges were acting well within the ethical rules.” As for the recusal motions, she said that “judges are unable to comment on matters currently pending before the court.” The new filings are the next stage of a campaign to portray judges who rule against the government or criticize its litigation tactics “as biased actors whose rulings can and should be discounted,” said Stephen Vladeck, a law professor at Georgetown. Asked for comment, a Justice Department spokesman pointed me to a statement issued last week in connection with the recusal motions in Minnesota. “A judge who has publicly taken a political side on the issue of enforcing our nation’s immigration laws cannot then preside over a case concerning one of the Justice Department’s key immigration enforcement initiatives,” the statement said. Vladeck is the author of the annual foreword to the issue of The Harvard Law Review devoted to the last Supreme Court term, which will be published shortly. Most of that long article, “The Court Against the Courts,” is devoted to an assessment of the Supreme Court’s tense and troubled relationship with the lower courts. Got a news tip about the courts? If you have information to share about the Supreme Court or other federal courts, please contact us. But it also addressed the administration’s attacks on federal trial judges. “The Supreme Court isn’t responsible for that campaign, but it has made it much easier for the Trump administration to wage it,” Vladeck told me. “It has said nothing about executive defiance of lower courts or the other attacks we’ve seen on the federal judiciary.” Indeed, he added, the justices are more apt to chastise lower-court judges for failing to divine the meaning of their cryptic emergency orders favoring Trump than to defend their colleagues from the administration’s declaration of war. Jack Goldsmith, a law professor at Harvard and a former Justice Department official in the Bush administration, concluded that the new charges against Comey were technically flawed and a gross abuse of power. An election law expert told my colleague Charlie Savage that the administration’s conditional challenge to the certification of the results of the Alaska Senate race was “the worst complaint I’ve ever seen.” Mailbag This week’s question concerns federal court records, which are available on an expensive service called PACER (that is, Public Access to Court Electronic Records). It seems long since past due that PACER should be a free resource. At one time there seemed to be a push to allow access without charge. That effort seems to have stalled. Can you update readers of the newsletter? — Jim Dale The push for free access to what are, after all, public records has not only stalled, but is moving in the wrong direction. The federal courts’ administrative office announced in June that it would impose “a modest temporary increase” in fees, raising them to 12 cents a page from the current dime. By one estimate, the technology exists to drive the actual cost of retrieving court documents to essentially zero — about one half of one ten-thousandth of a penny per page. That helps explains how, according to that announcement, PACER generates $147 million a year. The new rate starts in January and is scheduled to last for five years. The judiciary says the money is needed to modernize and protect the database, which was hacked in 2020 and 2025. Even as it raised the per-page fee, it expanded exemptions for light users and maintained some caps. Judicial opinions remain free. There have been bipartisan efforts in Congress over the years to remove PACER’s paywall, but they have yet to yield results. The Supreme Court has taken a different approach from the rest of the federal judiciary. Where PACER is clunky and costly, its website is sleek and free. I would love to hear your questions on the law, the courts or whatever is on your mind. Send them my way at the-docket@nytimes.com. Closing Argument The botched attempt to execute Christa Pike in Tennessee last month made me wonder what the Supreme Court had said about repeated attempts to put a condemned prisoner to death. After Pike survived two doses of a drug meant to kill her, she was hospitalized, having sustained traumatic injuries. She is back in prison, awaiting word on whether the state will try again. The Supreme Court has only once addressed whether trying multiple times to execute prisoners offends the Constitution. It was in 1947, in the case of a Black youth named Willie Francis, who was convicted by a jury of 12 white men of murdering a white pharmacist in Louisiana. The electric chair meant to kill Francis failed, though not before subjecting him to what witnesses said was intense pain. When the case reached the Supreme Court, five justices said a second attempt was permissible. Justice Harold Burton, writing for the four dissenters, seemed incredulous. “Taking human life by unnecessarily cruel means shocks the most fundamental instincts of civilized man,” he wrote. Justice Felix Frankfurter voted with the majority but added a concurrence. “This court must abstain from interference with state action no matter how strong one’s personal feeling of revulsion against a state’s insistence on its pound of flesh,” he wrote. Francis was represented by J. Skelly Wright, who would go on to be a distinguished judge on the D.C. Circuit. He was, one of his former law clerks wrote recently, “one of the heroic cadre of Southern judges who desegregated all-Black schools after Brown v. Board of Education.” That former clerk, Greg Diskant, also described an extraordinary postscript in the Francis case. “Without telling his brethren on the Supreme Court (except for Justice Burton), Frankfurter began a remarkable, extrajudicial lobbying campaign on behalf of Willie Francis,” Diskant wrote, drawing on a law review article and a book. “He enlisted his Harvard classmate, a Louisiana lawyer named Monte Lemann, on a ‘strictly confidential’ basis to seek clemency for Francis from the governor.” The effort failed. “Not terribly surprisingly, Gov. Jimmie Davis declined to exercise clemency for a Black man convicted of killing a white man in Jim Crow Louisiana,” Diskant wrote. Francis was electrocuted on May 9, 1947, about four months after the Supreme Court ruled. A 1982 article in The DePaul Law Review was harshly critical of Justice Frankfurter. “Frankfurter’s attempt to gain clemency for Willie Francis,” the article said, “can only be recognized for what it was: a pitiful attempt by a jurist to assuage his conscience for allowing a youth to be put to death in the name of abstract principles of federalism.” Please send me your comments on judicial ethics, public records, the death penalty or anything else at the-docket@nytimes.com. See you next week. — Adam Read the original New York Times article

甲州选举上阵三席 马华参选议席增加一席
item.description: 马华甲州选举参选议席增加一席。国阵主席阿末扎希（右）星期四（10月29日）将候选人委任状移交给怡力区候选人骆慧茹（中）和马华总会长魏家祥（左）。（取自魏家祥脸书） 马来西亚国民阵线成员马华在马六甲州选举的再增一个州议席上阵，并由38岁的马六甲历史城市议员骆慧茹代表国阵参选怡力州议席。 马华总会长魏家祥星期四（10月29日）在国会媒体室召开记者会时透露，加上之前的马接再也和吉里望，马华这次州选将竞选三席。马华在2021年甲州选举赢得马接再也及吉里望。 他说，国阵与国盟星期四进行最后一轮的议席分配谈判时，国阵主席阿末扎希与国盟领袖进行最后讨论后，就议席分配作出调整，双方敲定由马华竞选以华族选民为主的怡力州议席。国盟参选议席也由之前宣布的七席减为六席。 怡力是民主行动党的传统堡垒区。初试啼声的骆慧茹，除了将对决民行党原任州议员林朝雁，也可能要面对同心党候选人拉昔迪的挑战。 国阵本届甲州选举原本竞选21席，包括巫统18席，马华两席和国大党一席。怡力由马华上阵后，国阵将竞选22席。 甲州国阵主席阿都拉勿夫上周五在马六甲宣布，国阵将在甲州选举竞逐21席，并计划将马华上届参选七席中的五席，转让国民联盟上阵。 延伸阅读 甲州希盟起诉甲州国阵政府委议员违宪 马六甲州选提名在即 希盟24日国阵28日宣布候选人 此举引发马华强烈反弹，魏家祥率领马华代表离席抗议，并下令马华甲州各级基层组织全面冻结参与国阵一切有关甲州选举的协调会议。 马华除了不满议席锐减，也不满国阵未事先与马华充分协商便公布候选人名单，以及擅自宣布马华上次甲州选举胜出的两名州议员继续在原区参选。根据程序，候选人即使原区参选，也须由马华内部决定后再提呈国阵协商，不能毫无协商就对外宣布。 阿末扎希介入协调后，并在星期二（27日）指双方会谈后达致正面效果。魏家祥则承认双方星期一（26日）深夜在吉隆坡磋商，但双方尚未达致共识，马华是否参选仍须由党中央领导层决定。 魏家祥星期三（28日）告诉记者，马华在甲州选举只在两国州选区竞选，并确定使用国阵标志竞选。 马六甲州选举将于本周末（31日）提名，11月14日投票。

item.title: From a Billionaires Tax to Abortion Rights, Voters Will Decide Policy
item.description: Supported by More than 140 statewide ballot measures will go before voters during the midterms. Here are the races we’re watching. By Maia Spoto and Leo Dominguez Voters on Tuesday will elect federal and state politicians to represent them, but they will also exercise the power of direct democracy, setting policy through initiatives that will shape abortion and transgender rights, taxation, even the conduct of voting and direct democracy itself. Voters will weigh in on more than 140 statewide ballot measures, nearly 40 of them related to elections. That’s a record, said Helen Brewer, who tracks statewide ballot measures for the National Conference of State Legislatures. Jump to browse all 2026 ballot measures Ballot measures provide voters an opportunity to weigh in directly, often on policies that their representatives don’t really want changed. Some of the initiatives were proposed by lawmakers, while others were written by voters. A handful of the proposals seek to regulate ballot measures, by raising the threshold of votes needed for their passage or expanding safeguards to keep lawmakers from altering voter-approved policy. The outcomes will serve as a reality check, offering “at least some insight into what the voters who turn out in that election think,” Ms. Brewer said. Here are some of the ballot measures worth watching: Voters in a few states will weigh in on ranked choice voting, “dark money,” or the expansion of voting rights. And voters in nearly a dozen states will decide on citizenship or voter ID requirements. This measure, which has drawn support from President Trump, would repeal open primaries, where voters can choose which party’s primary they want to participate in, and ranked choice voting, where voters rank their top four choices. It would also loosen campaign finance restrictions. Voters approved Alaska’s current system in 2020 and narrowly voted to keep it in 2024. Corporations, nonprofits and labor unions — defined under this measure as “artificial persons” — would be banned from doing business in the state if they contribute to political campaigns. Electric and gas utilities and many government contractors would be barred from making campaign donations under this measure. The right to vote would be restored to people convicted of felonies upon their release. The measure would also narrow restrictions on people deemed “mentally incompetent” by a court, requiring a specific finding that they don’t understand voting. Requirements for voters to present identification or bans on noncitizens voting will also be weighed in Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Kansas, Nevada, North Carolina, Ohio, South Dakota and West Virginia. During an election season that has been animated by class tensions, many voters will decide on initiatives to tax the rich. The first-of-its-kind measure would impose a one-time 5-percent tax on wealth for Californians with a net worth over $1 billion, with nearly all of the revenue going toward health care. Wealth taxes are imposed on the value of personal assets, even if they are not sold, rather than on income or the sale of assets like stocks, bonds and property. Voters are deciding whether to repeal a 9.9-percent tax on income over $1 million a year, recently approved by the state legislature. The “millionaires tax” is expected to pull in more than $3 billion annually. Washington currently doesn’t tax personal income. Voters in the county that contains Chicago will weigh in on whether Illinois should adopt an additional 3 percent income tax on millionaires. The results aren’t binding. A similar proposed constitutional amendment didn’t make it onto the ballot. A mid-decade redistricting blitz that began at the urging of Mr. Trump has spun into multiple ballot measures asking voters to rethink how their state’s congressional maps are drawn. The state constitutional amendment would remove limits on how state lawmakers draw voter maps for congressional races. It would clear the way for the Democrat-led legislature to take aim at the state’s last Republican district on the Eastern Shore before the 2028 election. Voters will decide whether to adopt a congressional map that was redrawn to boost Republicans by dismantling a Democratic district around Kansas City. The Supreme Court blocked use of the map in 2026, saying the map needed voter approval. The state constitutional amendment would limit congressional redistricting by requiring public meetings as well as the approval of an independent commission and the state’s top court before a map can be modified. An effort by Democrats to allow for redistricting ahead of 2028 failed to make the ballot. For the first time, voters will decide on ballot measures about the participation of transgender students in school sports. Voters will also weigh in on the right to abortion in several states. Testing voters’ views on transgender issues in a deep blue state, the initiative would bar transgender girls in grades 6-12 from playing on girls’ sports teams. It would require doctors to verify an athlete’s sex to determine which league the student is eligible to play on. The measure in another Democratic state would block gender transition surgeries for minors and prevent state or federal funding from being used for these surgeries. The state constitutional amendment would repeal a right to abortion and ban gender transition medical care for children, including puberty blockers and hormone therapy. Missouri voters had approved the right to abortion in a 2024 initiative. The initiative would overturn one of the nation’s toughest abortion bans, which imposes criminal penalties on doctors who perform abortions. Colorado, Arizona and Nebraska voters are also weighing restrictions on transgender students’ participation in sports. Virginia and Nevada voters will weigh in on establishing a right to abortion in their state constitutions. Voters in several states will weigh in on policy around energy, transportation and development. In many local races, voters will decide if data centers, the computing sites powering the artificial intelligence boom, have a place in their communities. The initiative would streamline development for large projects like housing, roads and power infrastructure by limiting the scope of environmental reviews, which often draw lawsuits. Supporters say it could help ease the state’s housing crunch, while opponents say it goes beyond housing and warn of its potential to usher in the construction of data centers. A right to sell or purchase natural gas would be added Colorado’s state constitution in a first-of-its-kind measure. The initiative, promoted by a conservative political nonprofit Advance Colorado, comes as the state’s Democratic legislature and governor are taking steps to limit the use of natural gas to reduce emissions. The measure would amend the state’s constitution to block a tax based on the number of miles driven in a vehicle, an idea promoted by proponents of user taxes to fund infrastructure projects. Voters in parts of California, Florida, Illinois, Kansas, Maine, North Dakota, New Jersey, Nevada, Ohio and Wisconsin will weigh in on greenlighting, banning or otherwise regulating the construction of data centers across dozens of local races. Voters in several states will set rules governing their own power to create new policy through ballot measures. The constitutional amendment would bar state lawmakers from repealing or amending voter initiatives, unless at least 80 percent of both legislative chambers agree and the voters approve. It would also prevent lawmakers from taking action to weaken citizen initiative and referendum powers. Voters would be blocked from creating ballot measures to legalize marijuana or other drugs in this constitutional amendment that designates that power only to state lawmakers. The state constitutional amendment would require some voter-initiated legislation dealing with taxes to get 60-percent approval to pass. Read the original New York Times article

item.title: Third-Party Spoilers, Long Fueled by Both Parties, Could Matter This Year
item.description: Sly maneuvering around third-party candidates is a time-honored, bipartisan tradition in politics. Democrats and Republicans alike have long stealthily tried to help little-known names on the ballot who might siphon votes away from the opposing party’s nominees. The issue has suddenly become a top midterm story line because of remarkable drama in Alaska, where Democrats carried out a gambit to place a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot, alongside a Republican senator with the same name. But several other midterm battlegrounds also have outsider candidates who could swing a close race. In Ohio, Republicans have spent more than $2.2 million to promote a socialist candidate in the state’s vital Senate race, aiming to pull votes from the Democratic nominee, former Senator Sherrod Brown. In Virginia, a Republican group has sent mailers highlighting the Democratic-leaning positions of a self-described “radical centrist” running as an independent in a competitive House race. And in Nebraska, both major parties are jockeying to help minor candidates peel votes away from Senator Pete Ricketts, the Republican incumbent, and his Democratic-backed independent challenger, Dan Osborn. With modern elections often decided by extremely thin margins and billions of dollars sloshing through campaigns, both parties have ample incentives and opportunities to gain an edge through mischief involving third parties. The jockeying around spoiler candidates is widely considered a legal yet shadowy part of political campaigning that has gone on for decades. The Sullivan episode in Alaska is far from the first time that multiple candidates with the same name have run for the same office, with the lesser-known one often deliberately trying to confuse voters. There was even an Eddie Murphy movie in 1992 based on the concept of his character’s winning a seat in Congress previously held by a deceased politician with the same name. Usually the actors propping up spoiler candidates are careful enough about wiping away their fingerprints that they do not get caught in the kind of uproar that Mary Peltola’s Senate campaign now faces in Alaska. After a New York Times report detailing how allies of Ms. Peltola, a Democrat, had recruited little-known candidates to try to stack the ballot, Gov. Mike Dunleavy of Alaska ordered an investigation into whether the Peltola campaign should face criminal charges or civil penalties, and President Trump demanded that she be removed from the ballot. Neither suggested a specific law that had been violated. “Ghost voters are a bad phenomenon, but it’s a phenomenon that’s been in American politics for decades,” said Benjamin Ginsberg, a prominent Republican election lawyer. “At this point there’s no legal violation. Coming when it does, it’s purely up to Alaska voters, who, after all, put both Dan Sullivans on the ballot with their votes.” He added, “The whole thing is clearly political.” History offers plenty of precedent of third-party candidates playing spoiler. Former Senator Jon Tester of Montana, a Democrat, won his first two elections with a margin of victory that was less than the vote total for the Libertarian candidates in those contests. In 2000 and 2016, the number of votes that left-wing presidential candidates received could have been enough to flip the results had they gone to the Democrats running in those years. It does not always work. Mr. Trump’s allies tried to engage in this when they encouraged Kanye West to run for president in 2024, in an effort to shave off some Black voters from Mr. Trump’s Democratic rivals. The musician failed to get on the ballot in most battleground states. Usually, the third-party candidates are relatively innocent bystanders to the political drama swirling around them. This year in Ohio, Greg Levy, a member of the Party for Socialism and Liberation, is making a long-shot run for the Senate, his first bid for public office. He has raised about $132,000 mostly from small donors, is still working full time as a mover and is squeezing in his campaign stops in the evenings. So it came to his great surprise when a shadowy Republican group began what has become a nearly $2.3 million campaign to promote him to Democratic voters, mostly through mail and text messages, funded by a weeks-old super PAC with ties to Mr. Trump and Ohio Republicans. The group is itself entirely funded by a Republican group that regularly meddles in Democratic politics. “Say yes to the revolution,” one piece of mail pushing for Mr. Levy reads. “Vote Greg Levy for U.S. Senate.” Mr. Levy, 49, said in an interview that he opposed on principle the idea “that billionaires subvert the democratic process.” “I’m the only candidate that’s running that openly opposes political donations, period,” Mr. Levy said. “We want money out of politics, and we need to have an honest political system.” Republicans are trying to help Mr. Levy because polls show that the top of the ticket is a tight race between Senator Jon Husted, a Republican, and Mr. Brown, a Democrat trying to return to the chamber. In a contest that has drawn nearly $500 million in advertising spending so far, the money for the texts and mail on Mr. Levy’s behalf is a relative pittance. Ohio Democrats are aiming to help their own spoiler candidate in the Senate race. The state Democratic Party and Mr. Brown’s campaign have sent mail promoting the Libertarian candidate, Bill Redpath, as “a proud supporter of gun rights” — an apparent attempt to appeal to Republican voters. Tony Wen, a spokesman for the Ohio Democratic Party, declined to comment on the Redpath mailers. Mr. Redpath did not respond to messages. It is often hard to tell before an election how many voters are attracted to third-party candidates. The polling is complicated because research has shown that simply including a third-party candidate in a poll can lead to a drastic overstatement of their support, while not including them forecloses on voters’ opportunity to demonstrate any support for them. Pollsters typically err on the side of not including these minor-party candidates, largely because the candidates have not historically received much support. In 2024, third-party presidential candidates drew less than 2 percent of the vote nationally. This year, most of the late spending to help third-party candidates has come from groups that will not have to disclose their donors before Election Day. One such group, Our Heritage Matters, revealed last week that it had spent $340,000 to help Libertarian candidates in Senate races in Iowa and Kansas as well as in six House contests. In New Jersey, Republicans have tried to elevate a mysterious candidate named Seamus O’Toole. He is on the ballot in the House district where the Republican incumbent, Representative Tom Kean Jr., is running for re-election against Rebecca Bennett, a top Democratic recruit. Mr. O’Toole’s party is listed as “Stop Israel’s Genocide” — a position that could catch the eye of left-wing voters. Mr. O’Toole did not respond to messages from The New York Times and has not responded to New Jersey news outlets that have tried to reach him. In Virginia, Matt Baker, a retired Marine from Norfolk, decided to run for Congress as an independent because he was dissatisfied with both parties. In an interview, he described himself as a “radical centrist” and said that he borrowed policy ideas from both parties. Yet only his ideas that align with Democratic views — that he believes in abortion rights and that the 2020 election was not stolen, among others — showed up in mail sent by a Republican group called Progressive Champions PAC that called him “the independent choice for Congress.” The other side of the mailer called the Democrat in the race, former Representative Elaine Luria, “a corporate candidate.” The House Democratic campaign arm, however, signaled to outside groups that they should spend money to call Mr. Baker “a staunch supporter of the 2nd Amendment,” a detail reported earlier by Axios. Mr. Baker was not pleased to be used this way. “It makes me mad as hell,” he said. “They didn’t coordinate with me. They’re only telling half my story. I am a retired Marine, 28 years of service, and I think integrity is incredibly important. These shadowy people are going around trying to use me to trick people.” Other potential spoiler candidates are more sanguine about their situation. Two years ago, Lynn Chapman, a conservative political activist from Sparks, Nev., earned 5 percent of the vote as the Independent American Party candidate in Nevada’s Second Congressional District. It did not matter much, since Representative Mark Amodei, a Republican, won re-election by 19 percentage points. But this year Mr. Amodei is retiring. The race to succeed him is competitive. And Ms. Chapman is back, this time with some Democratic support. She is well aware that her vote total could be enough to swing the result to the Democratic nominee, Teresa Benitez-Thompson. Ms. Chapman, 77, said that, given the choice, she would rather see the Republican, David Flippo, an Air Force veteran, win the general election over Ms. Benitez-Thompson, a former state legislator. How would she feel if Ms. Benitez-Thompson won? “Oh, well,” she said. “Gee whiz, too bad.” Alaska’s Senate race is just the latest episode of Democratic and Republican candidates and their allies trying to elevate spoiler candidates to siphon off votes from their main rivals. This has been going on for decades in politics and Alaska is hardly the only example of it this year. If you are in a battleground state or district, have you gotten mail or texts or seen ads trying to boost candidates you didn’t know about? How do you feel about this legal but shadowy phenomenon? Ruth Igielnik contributed reporting. Kitty Bennett contributed research. Read the original New York Times article

item.title: 欧央行行长拉加德：基础通胀稳定，工资压力温和，融资条件已经收紧，不预设利率路径
item.description: 当地时间周四，欧洲央行行长克里斯蒂娜·拉加德（Christine Lagarde）在10月货币政策新闻发布会上宣布，管理委员会一致决定维持三大关键利率不变。在经历了中东地缘冲突引发的能源市场动荡后，欧洲央行选择在高度不确定的宏观环境下“按兵不动”。 拉加德在整场发布会中试图将市场的注意力集中在基础通胀的稳定上，并明确表示央行正在采用一种基于数据的观望策略。 拉加德在开场声明中直言不讳地指出了当前的宏观矛盾：“能源价格继续上涨，对通胀前景构成上行风险，对增长前景构成下行风险。” 淡化“二轮效应”：基础通胀稳定，工资压力温和 市场高度关注近期能源暴涨是否会引发更广泛的通胀失控。数据显示，欧元区通胀从8月的3.2%显著升至9月的3.8%，其中能源价格通胀从14.3%飙升至18.9%。剔除能源的核心通胀也从2.1%小幅攀升至2.3%。 然而，拉加德大量引用了底层数据来安抚市场对通胀全面扩散的担忧。她明确指出： “尽管能源冲击的全面影响仍在显现，但迄今为止基础通胀大体稳定，工资在此阶段也未显示出实质性反应。” 针对市场最为担忧的“工资-通胀”螺旋上升（即二轮效应），拉加德给出了关键的数据支撑： “工资压力仍然温和。第二季度雇员人均薪酬增长3.3%，低于第一季度的3.6%，而生产率上升有助于抑制单位劳动力成本增长。” 这一表态有力地打消了市场对央行因短期通胀反弹而被迫激进加息的恐慌。 融资条件显著收紧，增长前景偏下行，通胀前景偏上行 在经济增长方面，欧洲央行展现出了谨慎的态度。虽然最新数据表明欧元区经济在第三季度继续扩张，且服务业、制造业和AI相关的商业投资仍在提供支撑，但高利率的滞后效应正在显现。 拉加德在发布会上强调了金融环境的变化： “自我们上次会议以来，融资条件已经收紧，这可能拖累通胀和增长。” 她用具体数据描绘了信贷市场的寒意： “企业市场债务成本从7月的4.0%升至8月的4.1%，由于利率上升，抵押贷款需求大幅下降。” 关于未来的风险分布，拉加德给出了明确的指引： “增长前景的风险偏向下行，通胀前景的风险偏向上行。” 她特别提到了中东冲突以及俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争等地缘政治因素，警告称： “能源供应持续中断可能导致能源价格进一步上涨，这将拖累实际收入、支出和投资。” 拒绝预设路径，“逐次会议”决定未来 对于投资者最关心的未来利率路径和增长的可持续性想象空间，拉加德拒绝给出确定性的前瞻指引，而是将主动权交给了未来的经济数据。 “我们仍处于有利位置，能够应对当前高度不确定性。”拉加德重申了央行的政策框架： “我们将采用依赖数据、逐次会议的方式来确定适当的货币政策立场，我们不预先承诺特定的利率路径。” 她补充道，未来的利率决策将基于三大支柱：“对通胀前景及其周围风险的评估”、“基础通胀动态”以及“货币政策传导力度”。 在发布会的最后，拉加德向市场传达了央行的底线： “我们准备在职责范围内调整所有工具，以确保通胀可持续地稳定在我们的中期目标，并维护货币政策传导的顺畅运行。” 拉加德新闻发布会原文翻译： 下午好。我和副行长欢迎各位参加我们的新闻发布会。 管理委员会今天决定维持欧洲央行三大关键利率不变。 能源价格继续上涨，对通胀前景构成上行风险，对增长前景构成下行风险。尽管能源冲击的全面影响仍在显现，但迄今为止基础通胀大体稳定，工资在此阶段也未显示出实质性反应。 能源冲击的幅度和持续时间增加，以及对间接效应和二轮效应的影响，可能推高通胀并压低增长。 自我们上次会议以来，融资条件已经收紧，这可能拖累通胀和增长。我们致力于制定货币政策，以确保通胀在中期稳定在2%的目标。 我们仍处于有利位置，能够应对当前高度不确定性。我们将采用依赖数据、逐次会议的方式来确定适当的货币政策立场。特别是，我们的利率决策将基于我们对通胀前景及其周围风险的评估，并结合即将公布的经济和金融数据、基础通胀动态以及货币政策传导力度。我们不预先承诺特定的利率路径。 今天作出的决定已在我们网站发布的新闻稿中列明。 我现在将更详细地阐述我们如何看待经济和通胀的发展，然后解释我们对金融和货币条件的评估。 经济活动 最新数据表明，欧元区经济在第三季度继续扩张。服务业在中东冲突初期走弱后已经复苏。制造业、数字服务和出口正受益于人工智能相关商业投资。政府在基础设施和国防方面的支出也在支撑经济活动。这些因素应继续支撑近期增长。与此同时，能源价格重新上涨打击了消费者信心，融资成本上升可能拖累增长。 8月失业率仍为6.4%。就业和劳动力增长仍然低迷，而生产率已逐步回升。 中期内，能源价格逐步下降和劳动力市场稳健所推动的信心和实际收入复苏，应会提振国内需求。人工智能相关活动投资以及政府在基础设施和国防方面的支出也应继续支持增长。随着外需增强，出口增长应会加快。 提高潜在增长需要结构性改革，并且必须以健全的公共财政为支撑。财政可持续性是更广泛经济稳定的关键锚。对能源冲击的财政应对应是临时性、有针对性和量身定制的。简化并协调欧盟单一市场规则、加快能源转型以及完成储蓄与投资联盟，是使我们的经济更有活力和韧性的关键基石。随着数字欧元法律框架的达成进程进入最后阶段，我们重申尽快就单一货币一揽子方案达成协议的重要性。 通胀 通胀从8月的3.2%升至9月的3.8%。能源价格通胀显著上升，从8月的14.3%升至18.9%。柴油和汽油价格在9月创下新高，部分反映了炼油利润率上升。剔除能源的通胀从8月的2.1%升至9月的2.3%。食品价格通胀从1.1%升至1.3%。服务通胀从8月的3.0%升至9月的3.2%，而商品通胀从1.2%降至1.1%。 基础通胀指标大体稳定，但定价链早期阶段显示出上行压力。工资压力仍然温和。第二季度雇员人均薪酬增长3.3%，低于第一季度的3.6%，而生产率上升有助于抑制单位劳动力成本增长。我们的前瞻性工资追踪指标显示，2026年剩余月份协商工资增长将在2.5%至2.8%之间波动，并在2027年前三个季度平均为2.6%。较短期限的通胀预期已经上升，但多数长期通胀预期指标仍约为2%，支持中期通胀稳定在目标附近。 能源价格涨幅已超过欧洲央行工作人员9月预测中的基线路径。这可能在近期进一步推高通胀，并使整体通胀在未来几个季度远高于目标。此后，能源通胀下降以及更高利率的影响，应支持通胀回归目标。 风险评估 增长前景的风险偏向下行。这尤其源于中东冲突以及俄罗斯对乌克兰不正当战争的最新事态发展。能源供应持续中断可能导致能源价格进一步上涨，且上涨时间比目前预期更长。这将拖累实际收入、支出和投资。全球金融市场情绪恶化或全球债券市场溢出效应加剧，可能收紧融资条件，从而抑制需求。财政不确定性也可能进一步收紧融资条件并削弱信心，从而降低消费和投资。主要经济体之间贸易紧张局势重燃，可能进一步扰乱供应链、减少出口并削弱消费和投资。相反，如果经济和能源市场比预期更快地适应持续冲突造成的扰动，或者这些冲突得到可持续解决，增长可能高于预期。此外，欧元区企业采用新技术、政府在基础设施和国防方面的支出，以及提高生产率和完成欧盟单一市场的改革，可能比预期更多地推动增长。 通胀前景的风险偏向上行。这尤其源于中东冲突以及俄罗斯对乌克兰不正当战争的最新事态发展。能源冲击可能进一步加剧，其对其他价格和工资的影响可能比目前预期更强。尤其是天然气价格，如果供应进一步中断，或者异常寒冷的冬季恰逢低库存水平，可能上涨。能源价格保持高位的时间越长，就越可能通过间接效应和二轮效应推高更广泛的通胀。贸易紧张局势重燃可能导致全球供应链更加碎片化，削减关键原材料供应，并加剧欧元区经济的产能约束。极端天气事件——可能因“厄尔尼诺”条件加剧而强化——以及更广泛的气候和自然危机持续发展，可能比预期更多地推高食品价格。相反，如果持续的地缘政治冲突得到可持续解决，或者能源价格上涨带来的间接效应或二轮效应比预期更不明显，通胀可能低于预期。更加波动且风险厌恶的金融市场，加上更高的长期利率，可能拖累需求，从而降低通胀。 金融和货币条件 自我们上次会议以来，金融条件已经收紧。利率普遍上升，而股价下跌。 企业市场债务成本从7月的4.0%升至8月的4.1%，而银行对企业贷款利率仍为3.8%。银行对企业贷款增长从7月的4.4%放缓至8月和9月的年率4.2%，而公司债券发行在9月以年率4.2%增长，高于8月的3.8%和7月的3.5%。正如我们最新银行贷款调查所报告，第三季度对企业贷款的信贷标准收紧，银行称担心其客户面临的经济风险。尽管库存和营运资金的融资需求上升，企业贷款需求仍下降，尤其反映了更高利率的影响。 抵押贷款利率从7月的3.5%升至8月的3.6%，而抵押贷款增长在9月小幅降至3.0%。第三季度抵押贷款信贷标准保持不变，而由于利率上升，抵押贷款需求大幅下降。 结论 管理委员会今天决定维持欧洲央行三大关键利率不变。我们致力于制定货币政策，以确保通胀在中期稳定在2%的目标。我们将采用依赖数据、逐次会议的方式来确定适当的货币政策立场。我们的利率决策将基于我们对通胀前景及其周围风险的评估，并结合即将公布的经济和金融数据、基础通胀动态以及货币政策传导力度。我们不预先承诺特定的利率路径。 无论如何，我们准备在职责范围内调整所有工具，以确保通胀可持续地稳定在我们的中期目标，并维护货币政策传导的顺畅运行。 本文来自华尔街见闻，欢迎下载APP查看更多

item.title: He’s Photographed Every Magazine Cover You’ve Seen Lately
item.description: Sandra Bullock has posed for dozens of magazine covers over the course of her Hollywood career. But a cover shoot this year felt different. For this one, there was no wind machine, no slinky, backless number. Instead, styled in a modest plaid dress, Bullock was invited to step into an olive-green diorama and handed a broom. Behind the camera for the unusual shoot for Interview magazine was Szilveszter Makó, a Hungarian photographer whose painterly portraits inspired by his home country’s folklore have lately become inescapable in the fashion world and on social media. On Instagram last week, Jo Ellison, the editor of How to Spend It, The Financial Times’s glossy style magazine, posted a collage of Makó’s covers of Bullock, Emma Corrin, Gigi Hadid, Hunter Schafer and Daisy Edgar-Jones. Those came out in just the last few months. “How many more covers is Szilveszter Makó doing this season?” she wrote. A few days later, American Vogue unveiled its November cover star: Jenna Ortega, photographed by Makó. Then came Alicia Keys for Vogue Italia. The attention is “kind of unbelievable,” Makó, who is based in Milan, said during a visit to New York City in September. “I never imagined that there actually will be this much interest.” His magazine covers and brand campaigns are quickly recognizable for a collection of motifs: painted fish, flames, utensils and a dark cabin, to name a few. The images are muted and surreal: Elle Fanning in a voluminous dress, served on a giant dinner plate; Rama Duwaji standing in exaggeratedly pointy pumps beside an illustrated cat and chair that look as if they’ve leaped out of “Goodnight Moon.” “You step into Szilveszter’s brain when you step onto his set,” Bullock wrote in an email. “And that world was painted and constructed long before I showed up.” The images have broken through as some people have grown tired of seeing flawless celebrity faces against seamless backdrops. More and more, people crave texture, personality and signs of slight imperfection — even if these, too, have been painstakingly and deliberately created. This explains why Makó, 35, with his idiosyncratic tastes, is seemingly as booked and busy as Juergen Teller or Annie Leibovitz. “There’s an interest in flatness and painting and drawing in his work, which is in some ways not photographic,” said Emily Keegin, a photo editor and creative consultant who has directed magazine cover shoots featuring Ariana Grande and SZA. “And I think that aligns with where we are as a reaction to A.I. and a distaste for anything that’s hyperdigital.” Makó has become so well known for what Keegin calls his “heavy fingerprint” that last month he opened “Bauhaus Ballet,” an immersive experience in downtown Manhattan. The temporary exhibition, akin to the sort dedicated to van Gogh and Klimt, invited fans to step inside his sets. As celebrities, actors and members of the fashion world began to file in for the opening reception, they were offered glasses of Champagne by a row of hands protruding from behind curtains. Further inside, Makó was still making tweaks, pacing one of the galleries with a plastic bag of Kentucky bluegrass seed, which he sprinkled along the base of rustic plantings meant to evoke the Hungarian countryside. Makó, who tends to avoid interviews unless they are conducted as written exchanges, hesitated at first to speak with a New York Times reporter in person. But a couple days after the opening reception, he was back in the gallery space ready for a conversation. When it comes to creating images, “we are fighting always for perfection,” Makó said. “Everything needs to be the best possible. But there are limitations.” As an audio recording of the actress Gwendoline Christie reading a translation of a 19th-century Hungarian poem played on a loop, a line stretched down the block to get into the exhibition, which was produced with the Cultivist, an organization for art enthusiasts, and Capital One. Some visitors who filtered in recognized Makó, who on this day had a neat beard and wore a maroon baseball cap, and lingered nearby to eavesdrop. Growing up in Lillafured, Hungary, Makó spent two years attending a Waldorf school, where he learned to sew his own clothes and tend to plants and animals. Versions of his childhood home, a cabin of wattle and daub painted a dark brown, appear in some of his portraits as a statement headpiece. Early on, Makó said, he thought he might become a painter. But he had a formative experience while spending time in his mother’s hair salon, where he learned how to do edgy, “emo” cuts that he then photographed and posted on Myspace. Rather than photograph his subjects in the salon, Makó remembered telling them: “‘Your hair was iconic. Let’s go to the cemetery or the railway.’” “That was what we had,” he added. “The chicken coop.” That background touched off a yen for experimental images. He began booking shoots with fashion models who were just starting out, first in Hungary, then in Berlin and Milan, where he settled in 2013. “It’s very easy to shoot beautiful models,” Makó said. But he was more drawn to distinctive faces from smaller modeling agencies. As a college student, he studied photography but also took psychology courses. Makó said his “first big break” came three years ago, when GQ Italia asked him to photograph the actor Willem Dafoe for the magazine’s December 2023 “Men of the Year” issue. He put Dafoe in one of his house headpieces and posed the actor stooping in a box with a pillow and a spoon. Makó prefers to work with tangible objects as opposed to relying on computer-generated effects. He has come to realize that lots of other people like that, too. “I learned in the last few years that people do appreciate the materialism,” he said, “the fact that, actually, these things are existing.” (Makó said he used digital photo-editing tools but wouldn’t generate imagery from nothing.) In an email, Anya Taylor-Joy, who did a cover shoot with Makó in May, said she liked how the “2-D becomes tactile” in his images. There have been some creative differences. When Makó photographed the performance artist Marina Abramović last year, she came away frustrated. “He only wanted to do his ideas and vision that he prepared beforehand,” she said. “He didn’t realize that I am an artist, and I don’t want to be directed with no possibility for collaboration of my own.” When reached later for comment, Makó described himself as a longtime admirer of her work. “He was upset I didn’t want to put my head in a box as everyone else had done,” Abramović added. It’s rare for Makó’s subject to be a visual artist, too, with a competing aesthetic vision. But Abramović also touched on a criticism of Makó’s work that has grown louder as his photography has become more ubiquitous. Last week, after Ortega’s Vogue cover hit social media, some figures in the art and fashion worlds bristled at the familiarity of the image. Egregious to some was also that, in other photos, Ortega appeared in the same turquoise feathered dress that Hadid had worn in a spread for WSJ Magazine. “I need to collaborate with my stylists,” Makó said later by email. “If they like a piece, I will shoot it.” There is something paradoxical about the criticism, according to Elizabeth Goodspeed, an art director and a designer. “Makó is being commissioned precisely because his photographs look the way they do; expecting each new job to suddenly look different is like commissioning Yayoi Kusama to paint stripes,” she wrote in a recent essay. “It’s fine to let Makó be Makó!” Ellison, the How to Spend It editor, reflected on this, too, in an essay titled “The Curse of Overexposure.” Makó, who still feels new to the spotlight, said the harsh comments on social media were “heartless.” “I have, yes, a very distinctly particular way of how I take the pictures,” he said. “But for me, they don’t look the same.” Makó insists that he has not yet fully established his visual language, and that his style will continue to evolve. “They just need to be a little bit patient with me,” he added, “and give me some time.” There is rarely a stretch when Makó is not working or traveling, sometimes staying up all night, he said, to meet deadlines. A day off in Milan would probably find him at home in bed with his 9-year-old cat, Needle, shutters closed, rewatching “Harry Potter” movies or “The Queen’s Gambit.” “I want something that’s taking over my brain, and I don’t need to think,” Makó said. But, never one to be satisfied, he said he dreamed of photographing Tilda Swinton. He doubts, though, that he’ll ever feel the validation he craves: from his relatives, from former grade-school classmates, he said. This is partly because the world that his megawatt-star subjects inhabit doesn’t easily translate to life back home. It’s also because Makó is a vicious critic of himself. “The things that I really want, I will never have,” he said. “So it’s already a lost cause. Like being beautiful. I always wanted that.” Read the original New York Times article

item.title: 希盟拉土团 国阵联伊党 马国团结政府两大阵营各有谋算
item.description: 马来西亚反对党土团党主席慕尤丁（左八）等六名土团党国会议员，与副首相法迪拉（左九）为首的团结政府代表，星期四（10月29日）签署信任与拨款协议，同意合作至本届国会解散。（马新社） （吉隆坡综合讯）马来西亚团结政府成员国民阵线刚宣布第三次与反对党伊斯兰党合作出战马六甲州选举，首相安华领导的希望联盟隔天就与国阵及伊党的政敌土著团结党签署信任与拨款协议，两大阵营互别苗头意味明显。 《星洲日报》报道，巫统总秘书阿斯拉夫星期三（10月28日）在脸书贴文说，国阵与伊党主导的国盟当天签署谅解备忘录，正式组成战略合作伙伴联手参加甲州选举。这是两个政治联盟今年继柔佛与森美兰州选举后第三度合作。 国阵与国盟星期三（10月28日）下午签署谅解备忘录，正式组成马六甲州选举战略合作伙伴。出席签署仪式者包括国阵总秘书赞比里（左起）、巫统总秘书阿斯拉夫、国阵主席阿末扎希、伊党副主席依德里斯阿末和国盟总秘书达基尤丁。（取自巫统总秘书阿斯拉夫脸书） 出席签署仪式者包括国阵主席阿末扎希、国阵总秘书赞比里、巫统总秘书阿斯拉夫、国民联盟总秘书达基尤丁和伊党副主席依德里斯阿末。 阿斯拉夫当天在巫统最高理事会议后告诉记者，国阵与国盟已经同意共同发布联合竞选宣言。这份宣言由他与国盟总秘书达基尤丁签署，并由国阵主席阿末扎希见证。这份竞选宣言将于星期六（31日）完成提名后公布。甲州选举将在11月14日投票。 国阵与国盟高调宣布再次合作后，希盟为主的政府与13名反对党国会议员星期四（29日）签署信任与拨款协议。 根据协议，这13名国会议员将支持安华政府，直到国会届满。本届国会将在明年12月19日届满，政府可提前解散。 这13名国会议员也将支持2027年财政预算案，以及首相限任两届和律检分权等多项改革。团结政府则同意这些议员能获得与政府议员相同的选区发展拨款。 13人当中，包括土团党主席慕尤丁为首的六名土团党国会议员、六名之前支持首相安华而遭土团党开除的国会议员，以及睦达党麻坡区国会议员赛沙迪。 延伸阅读 传土团党有意和希盟再续前缘 历来第二次 希盟与反对党议员签信任拨款协议 这份协议由副首相法迪拉代表团结政府签署。负责法律及体制改革的首相署部长阿莎丽娜，以及安华的高级政治顾问扎富睿也出席签署仪式。 慕尤丁在签署仪式后告诉记者，土团党签署这份协议，与马六甲州选举毫无关系，也与希盟和土团党可能在雪兰莪达致类似协议毫无关系。 慕尤丁说，上述协议签署后，土团党仍留在反对党阵营，继续监督与制衡政府的。他说，协议将持续至国会解散为止。若其中一方违约，另一方就不必继续履行相关义务。 安华星期四在脸书指出，这份协议将有助于巩固政治稳定，确保政府施政得以延续。 上述13名国会议员加入支持政府行列后，安华在国会下议院222名议员中获得156名议员支持，超过148人的三分二门槛，为推动需要修宪的改革措施创造条件。 同属国盟成员的伊党和土团党去年底开始关系闹僵，伊党6月宣布终止与土团党的政治合作关系，但没有一方退出国盟。 目前，国会下议院剩下218名议员，因此四名前公正党议员此前宣布辞职。其中62人是反对党国盟阵营议员，包括伊党43人、国家宏愿党六人、支持国盟的土团党13人。 支持执政阵营的156名议员则包括希盟75人、国阵30人、砂拉越政党联盟23人、沙巴人民联盟七人、慕尤丁阵营的土团党议员六人、民兴党三人，以及睦达党、社会民主和谐党、沙巴立新党和马来西亚民族党各一人，另有八名独立议员。 这是马国政府第二次与反对党议员签署信任与拨款协议。时任首相依斯迈沙比里曾于2021年9月13日也与当时的反对党公正党主席安华等希盟四党领袖签署类似协议。 信任与拨款协议是英国议会制度里，弱势政府与反对派及独立议员达成的非正式合作协议。根据协议，当国会表决可能导致政府倒台的信任动议或预算案时，反对党及独立议员会投支持票或弃权以支撑政府，政府则以双方谈妥的政策让步作为回报。

Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
item.description: With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. By David Gritten Published: 2026-10-28T16:59:47Z Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show Partial results from Israel's general election show veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is leading his rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, but is still short of a majority in parliament. With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies were on track to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc were set for 48. Both leaders have said they will try to form a governing coalition. Arab-led parties, who are on course to win an unprecedented 19 seats, could emerge as kingmakers, but all but one of the Jewish parties have pledged not to work with them. With between 430,000 and 480,000 absentee ballots from soldiers and diplomats yet to be counted, it could still take a day or two for the final election results to emerge. Once they are confirmed, President Isaac Herzog will hold consultations with all the political factions and invite the leader whom he believes has the best chance of success to form a government - a process that could take weeks. If they fail, then ultimately there would have to be another election. During a meeting at his residence in Jerusalem, Herzog praised the 77.7% turnout in Tuesday's election, which was the country's highest in more than two decades. "It is a badge of honour for Israeli society, and it was remarkable to see how deep the desire for democracy is in Israel," he said. He added that he expected to receive the official results next week, after which he would begin discussions with every faction. "We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections. So, I expect everyone who comes here to come with an open mind." Both the prime minister and his main rival have insisted that they should be tasked with forming a governing coalition. Benjamin Netanyahu called for "a strong right-wing national government" Eisenkot declared that the public had "spoken in favour of change", after initial exit polls published by three Israeli broadcasters projected that his "Change Bloc" would emerge with between 52 and 53 seats in the Knesset, compared to 50 seats for Netanyahu's bloc. "The coalition of failure has lost the people's trust," he told supporters at Yashar's election headquarters in Tel Aviv. "I will work with my partners to ensure that the people's decision is translated into a Zionist government." Later, the broadcasters updated their exit polls, with two projecting that the rival blocs would be tied on 51 seats and one giving Netanyahu's bloc a narrow three-seat lead. Netanyahu then appeared at Likud's headquarters in Jerusalem and declared that his right-wing bloc had won a "great majority". "We must put in place a strong right-wing national government," he said. "It is forbidden, simply forbidden, to endanger Israel by forming a government that relies on anti-Zionist Arab parties." The leader of the left-wing Democrats party told its partners in Eisenkot's bloc on Wednesday that there was an "opportunity to form a change government in partnership" with the Arab parties and replace Netanyahu's coalition. "We have no future here if we don't stop being afraid. And if we don't put an end to racism," Yair Golan wrote on X. The two Arab parties - the United Arab List and the Joint List - appear to be heading for record representation because of a strong turnout among Arab Israelis, who account for about a fifth of the population and often describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel. The chairman of the Joint List, which has talked of providing an electoral "safety net" for the Jewish opposition, said on Wednesday that it was "ready and prepared to pave the way to oust the Netanyahu government". "Change runs through a Jewish-Arab partnership - a genuine and equal partnership. Nothing less, and nothing more," Yousef Jabareen wrote on X. Gadi Eisenkot said the Israeli public had "spoken in favour of change" United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas, who served in a short-lived governing coalition formed after the 2021 elections, said on Tuesday night that he hoped "the numbers will work out and we, the Change Bloc and the UAL, can ensure that there are 61 Knesset seats". Tuesday's election was the first since the deadly Hamas-led attacks on Israel on 7 October 2023 and the wars that followed in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. It was also seen by Israelis as one of the most consequential in the country's history, because it could decide not just their leadership but whether the country continues on its current hardline, religious-nationalist trajectory. Key campaign issues included accountability for the security failures that led to the 7 October attacks, the conduct of regional wars, conscripting ultra-Orthodox Jewish men into the military, judicial reforms and Israel's international standing. item.title: 奢华定制折叠旗舰 三星W27在中国正式发布
item.description: 从整体设计来看，三星W27采用黑金配色方案，机身融入金色装饰细节，以突出系列一贯强调的高端定位。与全球版Galaxy Z Fold系列相比，W27在外观材质和包装内容方面进行了专属定制，更强调商务与收藏属性。硬件方面，W27配备8英寸可折叠内屏以及6.5英寸外屏，支持高刷新率显示。性能部分搭载高通最新旗舰移动平台，并配备大容量存储组合，以满足高端用户对于多任务处理和生产力应用的需求。影像系统方面，三星W27延续旗舰级配置，后置三摄组合包含高像素主摄、超广角镜头以及长焦镜头，可实现多焦段拍摄能力。折叠形态也为自拍、视频通话以及内容创作提供了更多使用场景。人工智能同样成为此次W27的重要卖点之一。新机搭载三星最新Galaxy AI功能，支持实时翻译、智能摘要、内容生成、图片编辑等多项AI能力，并针对商务办公场景进行了优化，帮助用户提升工作效率。续航方面，三星W27配备大容量电池，并支持有线及无线充电功能。在系统体验上，新机运行基于Android深度定制的One UI系统，充分利用大尺寸折叠屏优势，支持多窗口协同、多应用同时运行以及跨应用操作。作为三星面向中国高端市场打造的专属产品线，W系列历来定位高于普通Galaxy旗舰机型。此次发布的W27也延续这一传统，在保持Galaxy折叠屏旗舰核心硬件的基础上，通过专属设计、定制服务以及商务定位来吸引高端消费群体。随着W27正式上市，三星进一步完善了其在中国折叠屏市场的高端产品布局。面对来自华为、荣耀、小米和vivo等品牌的激烈竞争，三星希望借助成熟的折叠屏技术积累以及W系列长期建立的高端形象，继续巩固其在超高端折叠手机市场中的影响力。

item.title: Commodore 64C宣布回归：沿用1980年代原始模具 打造现代复刻版经典电脑
item.description: 据了解，新款Commodore 64C最大的亮点之一在于机身外壳将直接使用1986年原版机型的注塑模具生产。这些模具在沉寂数十年后重新投入使用，使得新产品能够最大程度还原当年经典设计的尺寸、结构和细节。项目团队表示，他们在过去数月中陆续收集到大量历史遗留库存，其中包括原版外壳模具、键帽模具以及部分当年未使用的零部件。为了确保产品质量，团队对这些老旧生产设备进行了修复和现代化改造，使其能够满足当前制造标准。与许多仅依靠模拟器运行经典软件的复古产品不同，新版Commodore 64C被定位为真正可运行原生C64软件和游戏的平台。开发团队强调，他们希望打造的不只是一个怀旧收藏品，而是一台兼具历史价值和实际可玩性的完整电脑。新机将在保持经典米白色外观和标志性键盘布局的同时，引入现代接口和改进设计，以方便连接当代显示设备和外部配件。官方表示，用户既可以体验上世纪80年代的软件生态，也能够更方便地将设备融入现代家庭环境。Commodore 64最初于1982年推出，凭借相对低廉的售价、大量游戏和软件资源以及强劲的硬件性能迅速风靡全球。该产品后续累计销量达到数千万台，被广泛认为是历史上最成功的单一电脑型号之一。1986年推出的Commodore 64C则采用更加现代化的纤薄机身设计，并成为许多玩家心中最具代表性的C64版本。近年来，随着复古游戏和经典计算设备收藏热潮持续升温，大量厂商纷纷推出怀旧主机和复刻产品。然而，能够直接采用原始生产模具进行制造的案例极为罕见。因此，此次Commodore 64C复刻计划一经公布，便迅速引起复古计算机社区的广泛关注。项目团队表示，新版Commodore 64C不仅面向长期收藏者，也希望吸引年轻用户了解计算机历史的发展轨迹。对于许多经历过家庭电脑黄金时代的用户而言，这款产品不仅是一台电脑，更是一段数字时代早期记忆的重新回归。

item.title: 俄出口中心将坦桑尼亚列为非洲方向优先市场之一
item.description: 克列托夫出席了俄罗斯—坦桑尼亚商业理事会扩大会议。会议讨论了两国贸易、经济、投资及交通物流等领域的合作发展问题。克列托夫表示，俄罗斯出口中心将非洲视为重点业务方向之一，而坦桑尼亚在其中占据特殊地位。他指出：“从经济规模和发展潜力来看，坦桑尼亚有望成为东非和南部非洲地区的核心国家。俄坦两国合作势头良好，双边贸易持续增长，俄罗斯出口中心集团也积极参与其中。并且，在2026年，我们支持了近70家俄罗斯企业向坦桑尼亚出口产品，出口额超过2000万美元。”克列托夫强调，除了推动现有供货，保障两国投资合作同样重要，特别是在基础设施和自然资源领域。俄罗斯出口中心是一家支持非原材料、非能源产品出口的国家机构，为俄罗斯各行业企业开拓国际市场的各个阶段提供金融和非金融支持。该中心还承担着保障和实施“俄罗斯制造”计划的主要职能。第三届俄罗斯-非洲峰会暨经济和人道主义论坛于10月28日至29日在莫斯科举行，俄罗斯卫星通讯社是本届峰会和论坛的信息合作伙伴。
item.source: 俄罗斯卫星通讯社中文·最新

item.title: 《GTA6》剧情目标披露：双主角都想退出犯罪共同生活
item.description: 这也不难理解。R星显然希望在游戏发售前对叙事细节保密，不想剧透。不过，一篇有关本作的全新深度报道，让人们对杰森和露西亚的旅程有了更清晰的认识：两人似乎都希望告别犯罪生活。《Edge》杂志刊登了一篇关于《GTA6》的长篇专题报道，探讨了这款新作的多个方面，其中也包括游戏的叙事。据报道，杰森和露西亚的最终目标是金盆洗手。这让人们得以从不同角度理解，推动这两位系列新主角不断前进的究竟是什么。这可能意味着本作将与《给他爱5》有所不同。在前作中，金钱、物质财富和权力都在几位主角各自的故事里扮演着重要角色。而在《GTA6》中，R星似乎正在探索一些更加个人化的主题。工作室负责人罗布·纳尔逊承认，许多玩家将《GTA》系列视为一种权力幻想，但他表示，杰森和露西亚追求的不仅仅是这些。金钱依然是驱使他们行动的因素之一，但两人似乎对自己的人生以及彼此的关系抱有更大的期待。R星此前曾在《荒野大镖客：救赎2》中探索过类似理念，尤其体现在亚瑟·摩根的挣扎上：究竟是把钱花在自己身上，还是用来养活营地里的其他人。纳尔逊表示，《GTA6》将在这一概念的基础上继续深入，让主角拥有比单纯积累财富更细腻、更复杂的动机。对杰森和露西亚来说，两人的关系似乎正是这些期待的核心。游戏开场时，他们已经在一起，并且“想再给这段关系一次机会”。自游戏公布以来，两人那种受到邦妮与克莱德启发的搭档关系一直备受关注，但R星似乎还希望探索犯罪活动之外的生活，包括他们想要共同创造怎样的未来。当然，杰森和露西亚能否真正逃离犯罪世界，仍有待观察。鉴于该系列以往的故事走向，告别这种生活恐怕不会一帆风顺。这或许会在他们渴望的生活与实现目标所必须采取的行动之间，制造出一场颇具看点的冲突。《Edge》杂志对《GTA 6》的深度报道还披露了更多内容。报道公开了12张全新截图，也进一步展示了莱昂尼达地图的庞大规模——开发人员至今仍在发现一些自己此前从未见过的新区域。

item.title: US bans Chinese labs from testing electronics ahead of Trump-Xi meeting
item.description: The FCC measure targets testing facilities with alleged PLA ties, giving US labs until December 2028 to expand capacity. Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr has spearheaded the agency’s crackdown on Chinese technology companies. Photo: Reuters The United States on Thursday banned all Chinese laboratories from testing electronic devices destined for the US market, just weeks before US President Donald Trump is due to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) voted to bar testing laboratories and certification bodies in China and other economies that lack a “mutual recognition agreement” or reciprocal trade agreement with the US. “This is consistent with President Trump’s broader effort to restore balance and fairness with respect to America’s dealings with foreign nations,” said FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. “We are only allowing test labs to be based in the US or in reciprocal economies.” The ban would take effect in December 2028, giving domestic labs more than two years to expand their testing capacity. According to the FCC, more than 80 per cent are tested in facilities in China that the agency describes as “bad labs”. “Some of those labs themselves were linked or controlled by or tied to the PLA [People’s Liberation Army], so not necessarily the most trustworthy,” Carr told TBPN, a technology-focused online network, in August. An employee works at Ji’an Xiechuang Electronic Technology in Jiangxi province, China. Photo: Reuters The low profile US regulatory agency has emerged as one of the Trump administration’s most aggressive agencies targeting Chinese technology companies, even as other departments, including Commerce and Treasury, have adopted a more restrained approach. Under Carr, the agency has adopted a two-track approach, targeting specific Chinese companies while imposing broader bans on entire product categories and tightening supply-chain restrictions. Last week, it blocked two devices – a dashboard camera and a wireless video transmitter – containing chips made by Huawei Technologies subsidiary HiSilicon, arguing that they were “designed for the surveillance market”. In July, the agency announced bans on imports of new Chinese robots and power inverters, citing threats to US national security and supply chain vulnerabilities. “The networked capabilities of advanced robotic systems create extensive vulnerabilities and vectors for attacks that can manipulate the data and physical operation of the advanced robotic system,” the FCC notice said. In April, the agency advanced a proposal to bar three Chinese telecoms operators – China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom – from operating data centres in the US. The actions were followed by restrictions on new models of consumer routers in May. It also sought to prevent Hong Kong telecoms carrier HKT International from operating in the country, with Carr declaring that “CCP-controlled entities that pose national security risks to our country cannot connect to our telecom networks”. The measures came after a broader crackdown in December last year, when the FCC introduced restrictions across several sectors, including a sweeping ban on imports of new Chinese drones. After holding its fire for nearly a year, China retaliated in August by imposing tighter export controls on drones and related technologies, sanctioning US testing firms and launching its first national security investigation related to foreign trade. The tit-for-tat tech measures are in addition to an already crowded field of actions involving tariffs, export controls and the blacklisting of each other’s companies. By Nayan Seth Sections: News / US / China / Science & Technology | Topics: US-China relations, China Telecom, United States, China, Huawei Technologies, China Unicom, 2026 Xi-Trump summits, Diplomacy, US-China tech war, Hong Kong, Brendan Carr, Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, HiSilicon, Federal Communications Commission (US), China Mobile Short link: https://sc.mp/yzd7m Read the original article on SCMP

item.title: 政府就宏福苑火災鞠躬道歉 房屋局局長何永賢請辭承擔政治責任
item.description: 政府今日(29日)公布宏福苑火災獨立委員會報告，指就大埔宏福苑大火造成168人死亡，影響1,984個家庭，深感難過，向災民及廣大市民道歉。其後行政長官連同7名司局級官員隨即一同鞠躬道歉。 政府稱，考慮到宏福苑大火發生在房屋局轄下獨立審查組的負責統籌範圍，房屋局局長應承擔政治責任，而房屋局局長何永賢昨日(28日)已提出請辭，並獲接納。何永賢的職務今日起停止，由財政司副司長黃偉綸兼任房屋局局長。政府已報請中央，建議免除何永賢的職務。何永賢隨後發聲明表示，作為房屋局局長，願意為宏福苑的火災承擔政治責任，希望逝者可以安息，家人可以安心前行，早日走出傷痛。 對於何永賢餘下任期只有幾個月，現時請辭的問責任力度是否足夠？政府表示，綜合考慮所有因素，認為應由何承擔政治責任，無論任期有幾多，都要履行政治責任。當局又重申對事件深感難過，以政府之首的身份向災民道歉，未來再帶領政府作改革，不容許再發生同類事件。 被問到政府的道歉是否太遲，當局表示宏福苑大火後，政府即時的首要任務是拘捕疑犯及安置居民，認為現階段是適合的時候代表政府道歉，又指政府會從事件吸取教訓，加強公務員培訓。 至於為何發展局、勞福局及保安局局長不需要承擔政治責任，政府表示，是否承擔政治責任要考慮多方面因素，包括官員在事件的角色、其政策範圍與事件的關係、下屬的行事表現等。考慮到大火發生在宏福苑，屬於房屋局轄下獨立審查組的管轄範圍，雖然火災不涉及房屋局局長個人犯錯，但認為房屋局長應該承擔政治責任。 政府又指，對4個相關部門的不足及缺失，感到非常失望，因為他們沒有履行以民為本、及以結果為目標的施政理念，公務員敍用委員會將進行獨立調查。當局提到，公務員敍用委員會調查對象數目不小，估計約有40至50人，從部門最高至最低級的職員，都有機會被問責，會為敍用委員會提供全面自主權進行調查。

item.title: 五中全會審議通過決定 推進全面從嚴治黨
item.description: 中共第二十屆中央委員會第五次全體會議周一（26日）至周四（29日）在北京舉行，全會審議通過《中共中央關於持之以恒推進全面從嚴治黨若干重大問題的決定》。 全會強調，持之以恒推進全面從嚴治黨遵循堅持服務使命任務，堅持以黨的政治建設為統領，堅持全面從嚴，堅持問題導向，堅持守正創新，堅持以上率下，堅持依規治黨的原則。就持之以恒推進全面從嚴治黨作出系統部署，嚴格貫徹執行民主集中制，鍛造堪當民族復興重任的高素質幹部隊伍，建設上下貫通、執行有力的嚴密組織體系，馳而不息正風肅紀，堅定不移一體推進不敢腐不能腐不想腐，堅持制度治黨、依規治黨，完善黨和國家監督體系，壓緊壓實管黨治黨責任。 全會提出，全面從嚴治黨關鍵在從嚴治吏，必須貫徹新時代黨的組織路線，嚴格幹部教育培養、選拔任用、管理監督，建設一支政治過硬、本領高強、作風優良、紀律嚴明的高素質幹部隊伍。要堅持正確用人導向，推動幹部樹立和踐行正確政績觀，提高培養選拔優秀年輕幹部質量，加強幹部管理監督，全方位培養、引進、用好人才。黨的各級組織是全面從嚴治黨的主體，必須體系化推進各層級各領域黨組織建設，強化黨組織政治功能和組織功能。 全會號召全黨堅持不懈把全面從嚴治黨向縱深推進，不斷開創新時代管黨治黨、興黨強黨新局面。持之以恒推進全面從嚴治黨是全黨的共同政治責任。必須扭住管黨治黨責任制「牛鼻子」，健全各負其責、統一協調的責任體系，優化責任落實考評機制，對管黨治黨不力、出現嚴重問題的嚴肅追責問責。正風肅紀是全面從嚴治黨的有力舉措，一體推進不敢腐不能腐不想腐是全面從嚴治黨的重要方略和反腐敗鬥爭的基本方針，加強黨內法規制度建設是全面從嚴治黨的長遠之策、根本之策，必須進一步完善黨和國家監督體系，做實黨委（黨組）全面監督，完善紀檢監察工作雙重領導體制，推動黨內監督同各方面監督深度融合、高效聯動，發揮巡視綜合監督利劍作用。

item.title: 也门胡塞武装称沙特空袭塔伊兹省致12人死亡
item.description: 也门媒体报道，当地塔伊兹省两栋民宅星期四（10月29日）遭沙特阿拉伯空袭，造成至少12人死亡、三人重伤。图为一名公众在也门西南部塔伊兹省街上行走。（路透社） 也门媒体报道称，也门西南部塔伊兹省两栋民宅星期四遭沙特阿拉伯空袭，造成至少12人死亡、三人重伤。 也门胡塞武装控制的马西拉电视台报道称，沙特星期四（10月29日）空袭两栋位于塔伊兹省西部马克巴纳地区巴尔赫一带的民宅，造成上述伤亡。报道未提供更多细节。 截至目前，沙特和国际社会承认的也门政府尚未就此次空袭及人员伤亡作出回应。 延伸阅读 胡塞武装指沙特空袭酿14死 向亚丁机场发导弹反击 胡塞：埃及军事支持沙特等同于宣战 塔伊兹省俯瞰红海和曼德海峡，具有重要战略地位。胡塞武装与沙特支持的也门政府军在多条战线的交火日趋激烈，两者为争夺该省控制权而交战。 近期，沙特与胡塞武装互袭力度增强。沙特主导的多国联军加大对胡塞武装控制地区的空袭，胡塞武装则向沙特境内发动弹道导弹和无人机袭击。

item.title: The Rise of American Chenin Blanc
item.description: American chenin blanc is back and better than ever. Dozens of top California producers, intrigued by the grape’s potential, are now making superb chenin blancs, along with a scattered few producers in Oregon, New York and elsewhere. Even so, chenin blanc remains a modestly planted grape. Back in 2015, I wrote an article that predicted this return, perhaps jumping the gun by a few years. Since then, however, the number of producers making chenins has vastly increased, even as the amount of chenin planted in California has only risen by 15 percent or so since then, according to the Agriculture Department’s California Grape Acreage Report. It’s perhaps a concession to the downturn in wine consumption that plantings of chenin blanc have not increased more. Growers, understandably, are hedging their bets. So, while many more producers are making chenin blancs now than 10 years ago, most are making minute amounts. Regardless, this is great news for American wine drinkers. Chenin blanc is one of the world’s most versatile grapes, rivaled only by riesling in its ability to make profound wines that range from bone-dry to lusciously sweet. Chenin can make wonderful sparkling wines, too. More good producers making great wines is only the beginning, I hope, of a larger focus on chenin blanc in the United States. In May, I was able to taste more than two dozen small-production American chenins at Hella Chenin, a joyous festival celebrating the grape that was held in Berkeley, Calif., featuring many American chenins as well as those from South Africa, which, along with the Loire Valley of France, is a world center of chenin production. I recently went shopping for American chenin blancs in New York and found 10 bottles that I highly recommend. But the number of American chenin blancs I couldn’t find far exceeds those I recommend. Those include chenins from Littorai and Rhys Vineyards, which stand among the best American producers of pinot noir and chardonnay. They have now turned to chenin as well. Those wines are scarce and expensive. I also could not find more affordable bottles from Pax, Haarmeyer, Leo Steen, Rococo, Las Jaras, Matt Taylor, Matt Crutchfield, Minus Tide, Lo-Fi, Lang & Reed, Gail and Bow & Arrow. I’ve tasted them all and will vouch for any of their bottles. Chenin blanc wasn’t always so scarce. In the 1980s, chenin was the most widely planted white wine grape in California, with roughly 35,000 acres compared with about 4,100 acres today. Back then, most of those grapes were used to make cheap semisweet jug wines. Most were pulled out as California’s growers came to concentrate on a mere handful of grapes that accounted for both California’s finest wines as well as inexpensive knockoffs of those fine wines. Today, those making varietal chenin blancs tend to be ambitious producers intent on making excellent wines. If you’re curious about these wines, look in good wine shops, the sorts of places that don’t focus on mass-produced brand names. Despite the growing interest in the grape, it’s still an insider’s treat and relatively unknown in the larger wine world. Considering the difficulty I had in tracking them down, don’t be discouraged if you don’t find them immediately. I promise, they will reward patience. Here are the 10 wines, in order of price. Dashe Clarksburg Les Enfants Terribles Concrete Cuvée Chenin Blanc 2023, 12.5 percent, $26 I’ve always liked the wines from Dashe. They feel modest in the best possible way. That is, they do not impose themselves on you like big, slobbery dogs, but are catlike, brimming with details that reward careful observation. This chenin blanc from Clarksburg in the Sacramento River Delta is quietly enticing with subtly complex floral aromas and flavors. Lieu Dit Santa Ynez Valley Chenin Blanc 2025, 12.5 percent, $30 This is a superb wine, with all the paradoxes that good chenin blanc wines possess. It’s lean yet rich, dry with the impression of honeyed sweetness, floral yet saline — altogether lovely. Lieu Dit is a small négociant that specializes in Loire grapes grown in the Santa Barbara area. The Terraces Clarksburg Chenin Blanc 2024, 11.9 percent, $31 The Terraces is situated in Napa Valley and naturally grows and makes cabernet sauvignon. But it also roams far afield to make more esoteric wines like falanghina, riesling and this one, chenin blanc from the Clarksburg region. It’s lean yet sun-kissed, full of floral, honeyed flavors that leave a lasting impression on the palate. Sandlands Amador County Chenin Blanc 2023, 12.4 percent, $34 Chenin blanc has been a focus of Sandlands, Tegan Passalacqua’s label, which explores classic California grapes from old vineyards in the northern part of the state. Mr. Passalacqua, who by day is the winemaker at Turley Wine Cellars in Napa Valley, is one of California’s foremost vineyard and wine historians and a sensitive farmer and winemaker. His chenin blancs are always superb, and I particularly like the ’23 Amador County. It’s layered and complex, and will continue to evolve as it ages. Birichino Santa Ynez Valley Jurassic Park Vineyard Old Vines Chenin Blanc 2024, 13.5 percent, $35 After nearly 20 years in business, Birichino, founded by upstart alumni from Bonny Doon, has settled into a sort of middle-age reliability, making small quantities of excellent wines from Central Coast vineyards at fairly reasonable prices. This chenin is richer and fuller-bodied than many in this lineup. It’s made from older vines that, unusually, are planted on their own roots rather than grafted onto American rootstock, as is conventional. It’s lush yet dry and would match nicely with poultry or a richer fish like halibut. Ridge Clarksburg Heringer Chenin Blanc 2025, 13.2 percent, $36 Ridge Vineyards, which has been making wines for decades from all over California, issued its first varietal chenin blanc in 2024. The wine, made from Clarksburg grapes, shows Ridge’s characteristic careful approach. It’s fine and detailed, with filigreed floral and honeyed flavors that give the impression of sweetness even though the wine is dry. Maître de Chai Clarksburg Wilson Vineyard Sparkling Chenin Blanc NV, 11.5 percent, $37 Chenin blanc is the source for wonderful sparkling wines in the Loire Valley. Maître de Chai, a sort of micronégociant based in Berkeley, Calif., does great justice to those wines. This is elegant and refined, with gentle bubbles that flatter its yeasty, floral and honeyed flavors. Outward Paso Robles Highlands District Shell Creek Vineyard Chenin Blanc 2024, 12.5 percent, $37 This partnership of Natalie Siddique and Ryan Pace makes excellent wines from vineyards in and around the San Luis Obispo Coast in California. This lively, expressive wine comes from old vines of chenin blanc planted inland from the town of Paso Robles. It’s both fresh and rich, with an almost gritty texture that makes you want to go back for more. Aperture Clarksburg Chenin Blanc 2023, 12.2 percent, $38 Aperture is based in Healdsburg in the Dry Creek Valley. Its proprietor, Jesse Katz, specializes in cabernet sauvignon but also makes a range of other wines like this chenin blanc from Clarksburg. It’s bright and floral, with a pronounced citrus streak, well-balanced and textured. Hope Well Eola-Amity Hills Chenin Blanc 2025, 12 percent, $56 Mimi Casteel is one of wine’s foremost proponents of regenerative agriculture. To walk her vineyard is to feel you are in a thriving, complex ecosystem. Her Hope Well wines convey that same energy. She has added chenin blanc, a rarity in the Willamette Valley of Oregon, to her lineup of pinot noirs and chardonnays. This fresh young wine is complex and alive and ought to evolve beautifully with time. Follow New York Times Cooking on Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok and Pinterest. 谷歌市值创纪录蒸发5000亿美元 AI侵蚀营收
item.description: 这家谷歌母公司公布，第三季度不含合作伙伴分成的营收为1112亿美元，低于分析师预测。搜索及其他渠道的广告营收也不及预期，增速为五个季度来最慢。这项业务约占公司总营收的一半，也是为巨额AI投资提供资金的关键来源。摩根大通分析师Doug Anmuth等人在研报中表示，业绩和股价反应显示，对于投入数千亿美元建设AI基础设施的超大规模云服务商而言，一旦核心业务业绩令人失望，容错空间有多小。截至纽约时间上午9：35，Alphabet股价下跌13%，至281.37美元，市值蒸发5110亿美元。这跟竞争对手微软的表现形成鲜明反差。微软云业务增速超出华尔街预期，同时控制支出，推动股价上涨。谷歌首席商务官Philipp Schindler周三晚间在财报电话会议上表示，谷歌搜索中新推出的AI Mode标签页日益普及，对公司业绩造成了拖累。他表示，AI查询的“变现能力较低”，不过公司对此仍持乐观态度，并计划在搜索引擎的这一板块投放更多广告。多年来，谷歌高管一直认为，AI聊天机器人和相关功能不会大幅侵蚀其搜索业务。但随着消费者转向ChatGPT、Claude以及谷歌自身的AI功能，投资者担心这会冲击公司的核心盈利来源。Alphabet首席执行官Sundar Pichai面临的压力越来越大，他需要证明谷歌未来在数据中心、算力及电力等资源上逾1万亿美元的付款义务是合理的。Investing.com高级分析师Thomas Monteiro表示：“这个季度感觉像是Alphabet的关键时刻：要么Pichai及其团队解决AI变现问题，要么这家巨头就可能在不久的将来失去其在几项核心业务中的领先地位。”Monteiro表示，除非谷歌证明自己也能靠AI收费，就像过去靠搜索广告收费那样，否则它发布的每一份资本支出预测看起来都不太像是在展现雄心，而更像是一张账单。谷歌为自身及客户建设AI基础设施，推动资本支出升至纪录水平。公司正利用AI改造搜索引擎、YouTube和Gmail等广受欢迎的产品，但这些举措尚未带来投资者所期望的、足以证明其庞大支出合理性的营收。第三季度谷歌服务业务总营收963亿美元，低于预期的984亿美元。YouTube广告营收112亿美元，也低于预期。公司自由现金流连续第二个季度为负，为上市以来首次连续两季出现负值。Alphabet的股权投资也拖累了公司利润。这些投资录得87亿美元亏损，很大程度上源于Alphabet所持SpaceX股份。这与一年前的投资收益以及第二季度的巨额收益形成鲜明反差；第二季度的收益主要来自SpaceX和一家非上市公司的投资，后来确认这家公司是Anthropic PBC。Alphabet第三季度每股净利润为2.12美元，远低于华尔街预期的2.99美元。财报中的一个亮点是谷歌云，该业务被视为衡量公司AI产品和托管服务需求的重要指标。谷歌云营收307亿美元、利润111亿美元，均高于分析师预期的291亿美元和98亿美元。该业务的大客户包括Anthropic等在AI竞赛中与谷歌竞争的初创公司。

item.title: 《影之刃零》交卷 国产3A还能再造一个《黑神话》吗？
item.description: 游戏之外的热闹同样不少，多个相关话题登上热搜，《黑神话：悟空》（以下简称《黑神话》）制作人、游戏科学创始人冯骥也发文推荐，网友调侃，这是“村里的第一位大学生”给第二位送上祝福。业界对《影之刃零》有很多期待。《黑神话》之后，市场一直等待另一款能证明国产3A实力的作品，而《影之刃零》从媒体评分到玩家人数，再到销量预期，几乎每项表现都被放到了前者的参照系中。目前，《影之刃零》海外PC版媒体评分已经超过《黑神话》，但玩家评价仍有分歧，能否复制前者的销量和商业成绩，还有待市场检验。游戏行业分析师张书乐对第一财经记者表示，对于《影之刃零》来说开局不是巅峰，大众记忆往往只会记住第一是“黑猴”，很难记住第二，发售日只是第一步，真正的破圈还需要对照“黑猴”走通的路，继承并超越。游戏行业投资人对记者提到，《影之刃零》达到《黑神话》的销量很难，但首年1000万份的销量很有希望，游戏“独特、完成度不错”。评分超《黑神话》，玩家口碑分化正式发售前，业界对《影之刃零》就有诸多讨论了，有人比较其预购数，有人比较媒体评分。据数据分析网站Alinea Analytics统计，截至10月20日《影之刃零》预售销量已达50万份，预购收入约2400万美元（约合人民币1.6亿元），Steam愿望单数量达250万；以发售前70天为节点，其同期销量约为《黑神话》的73%。定价上，《影之刃零》延续了与《黑神话》相近的价格带：PC数字标准版268元、豪华版328元；面向收藏玩家的实体典藏版礼盒售价1199元，全球限量2万套。媒体评测则进一步抬高了玩家的期待。游戏评论汇总网站Metacritic显示，《影之刃零》PC版媒体均分为88分，高于《黑神话》PC版此前的81分。不过，玩家评分更加分化。截至发稿，《影之刃零》在Steam已收到超过3700条玩家评价，好评率约78%。在最早一批进入游戏的玩家中，有人认为它比《黑神话》更好玩、上手门槛更低，也有人对打击感、文案叙事和游戏节奏提出批评。在Sream社区的热评前列，有玩家反馈，“游戏序章体验较差，整体动作体验不错，但是砍怪的打击感飘飘的，游戏8-8.5分是有的，满分评价有点过，优缺点很明显。”这位玩家认为，国产游戏任重道远，很多细节方面与传统3A大厂仍有差距。有认真的玩家发表了约千字长文评价，认为《影之刃零》会是个好游戏，但自己因为一些原因退款了，包括人物对话的文案过于浅白而失去代入感、游戏节奏慢等等。首日评价还不足以为一款大型单机游戏盖棺定论，但也说明，游戏的玩家更多元，其反馈和媒体评测建立的大众期待并不完全相同，后续走向要看玩家的实际体验如何。《影之刃零》的卖点是一套带有中国功夫电影气质的动作体验。游戏由北京灵游坊研发，基于虚幻引擎5制作，构建了融合中式武侠与蒸汽朋克元素的架空世界。玩家扮演心脏遭受重创、仅余六十六天生命的剑客，在追杀与逃亡中揭开笼罩武林的阴谋。为了让这场武侠冒险成立，团队投入了大量制作资源。据灵游坊创始人兼CEO梁其伟透露，游戏总研发成本在3亿至4亿元之间。这与《黑神话》的总开发成本接近。发售前一天，梁其伟发文回顾开发过程：数千小时的动作捕捉，遍访中国城镇与山村进行3D扫描，并邀请广东舞狮大师、峨眉剑术大师、少林寺僧人分别指导舞狮、剑阵和拳法。由动作导演羊柳带领的武打动捕团队，也在甄子丹的顾问指导下，为游戏制作了大量攻击、防御、闪避、连招及处决动作。高投入开发背后有业内知名资本支持。腾讯是灵游坊的重要投资方之一，于2021年对其完成数亿元规模的战略投资，为《影之刃零》的3A级开发提供了关键资金与资源支持。此外灵游坊的早期投资方还出现过真格基金、网易资本、英雄互娱等。在《影之刃零》游戏的特别鸣谢名单中，出现了海内外游戏行业的“半壁江山”，包括腾讯高级副总裁马晓轶、游戏科学创始人冯骥、米哈游联合创始人刘伟、库洛游戏CEO李松伦、英雄游戏创始人吴旦、心动网络联合创始人黄一孟等人。一款国产3A的发售，牵动的不只是开发团队，还有正在关注这条赛道的同行。破圈难复制，国产3A需要更多辨识度对于《影之刃零》而言，绕不开的比较对象是《黑神话》。公开数据显示，《黑神话：悟空》全平台累计销量突破3000万份，其中Steam平台销量突破2300万份，收入超过11亿美元，刷新了多项国产买断制游戏纪录。《影之刃零》能否达到《黑神话》的成绩，成为关注焦点。有行业人士认为，《黑神话》的成功是现象级的：西游题材的认知基础、国产3A的突破意义，以及在此基础上的万众瞩目和破圈，占尽天时地利人和，共同构成了一个难以复制的市场窗口。后来者可以借鉴它的开发和发行经验，却很难原样复制那次破圈。投资人对记者表示，虽然《影之刃零》达到《黑神话》的销量有难度，但首年销售1000万份仍有希望。另有行业人士表示，游戏的预购表现不错，也积累了前期势头，接下来要看口碑能否支撑持续销售；如果最终销量能达到《黑神话》的一半，即1500万份，就属于巨大成功。张书乐对第一财经记者表示，大众往往更容易记住率先突破的作品，《影之刃零》要进一步破圈，需要找到自己的辨识度。他将其比作中国游戏行业的“第二颗星”：就像一支球队不能只有前锋，每个球星也都要有自己的绝技。在他看来，两款游戏的吸引力有所不同。《黑神话》借助中国古典神话和悟空IP打开市场，《影之刃零》则突出中国武侠动作大片，像一部蒸汽朋克版的游戏《卧虎藏龙》，有机会通过功夫题材吸引更多海外玩家。张书乐分析，仅仅从传播势能上看，《影之刃零》可以和《黑神话》旗鼓相当，发售首日的热度是一种体现。在游戏上线后，冯骥发文，提到和梁其伟在很多年前就认识，“殊途同归，我们都在某个时间点决定去做自己更喜欢的事情”。他认为，对中国的单机内容创作者来说，当下是一个更好的时代，也是一个更难的时代。好的一面是，中国拥有充沛的人才储备、巨大的本土市场与便捷的全球分发渠道，且单机不存在零和博弈，优质产品供给长期不足；但难的点在于，单机游戏开发周期较长、体验门槛较高、玩家见多识广，且新的娱乐方式层出不穷，争夺用户时间。后来者享受着《黑神话》打开的市场，也面对着被它进一步抬高的期待。过去两年，在《黑神话》之后，入局做3A游戏的玩家不少，包括《归唐》《湮灭之潮》《一盏秋声：锦衣卫》等中国自研单机项目陆续进入公众视野。有发行行业人士对第一财经记者表示，《黑神话》改变了国产单机的外部环境，无论是愿意为国产买断制游戏付费的玩家，还是头部厂商对单机领域的投入规模，以及行业的投资、宣发力度等等都得到了提升，更多的从业者在加入。他判断，2027-2028年会是一个单机游戏短期内的爆发点。过去几年陆续启动的一批项目，将在未来两年集中进入上线期。当更多作品走向市场，谁是下一个《黑神话》或许不再重要，更有意义的是，不同题材、不同团队的国产3A，能否各自找到玩家，并获得足以支撑下一部作品的回报？这才是对行业来说更良性的循环。

item.title: 欧洲银行称，前9个月净利润为11.6亿欧元，2025年同期为10.3亿欧元。
香港房屋局局长何永贤为宏福苑大火承担政治责任请辞
item.description: 香港特首李家超（左四）星期四（10月29日）在记者会上率领保安局局长邓炳强（左起）、律政司司长林定国、政务司司长陈国基、财政司司长陈茂波、财政司副司长黄伟纶与发展局局长甯汉豪向宏福苑大火灾民及广大香港市民鞠躬致歉。劳工及福利局局长孙玉菡也在场但未被摄入镜头内。（路透社） 在宏福苑大火事发近一年后，港府首次就事故道歉，并宣布房屋局局长何永贤为承担政治责任请辞。受访学者认为，此举展现了官方政治问责的精神，港人也关注会否有更多相关政府人员被追究责任。 宏福苑是在去年11月26日发生五级大火，导致168人死亡，成为香港近年最严重的火灾事故之一。特首李家超过后成立独立委员会调查事件起因、相关责任及提出防止类似事件再次发生的建议。委员会已于10月22日提交报告。 李家超星期四（10月29日）率领多名主要官员举行记者会，公布报告主要内容及政府跟进措施。他在记者会开始时说，作为行政长官及特区政府之首，他对事件深感难过，要代表政府向灾民及广大市民致歉。随后他与七名官员一同站立，在传媒镜头前深深鞠躬。 李家超指出，虽然宏福苑大火不涉及房屋局局长个人犯错，但考虑到宏福苑属于房屋局辖下独立审查组负责执行楼宇监管的物业，局长应承担政治责任。房屋局局长何永贤星期三（10月28日）向他提出辞呈，表示愿意承担政治责任，他已接纳其请辞，并委任财政司副司长黄伟纶兼任房屋局局长职务。 香港房屋局局长何永贤星期三（10月28日）向特首李家超请辞，表示愿意承担宏福苑火灾的政治责任。图为何永贤1月21日在香港立法会中发表讲话。（中通社档案照片） 房屋局局长在香港是政治任命职位，政治位阶处于特首、三位司长（政务司司长、财政司司长与律政司司长）及副司长之下，与其余各决策局局长同级，是特区政府的主要官员，相当于新加坡政府的部长。 延伸阅读 宏福苑大火问责 港房屋局局长何永贤请辞 戴庆成：香港工程监管为何一再失守？ 李家超说，除了政治问责，下来也将追究相关公务员的行政责任。他引述独立委员会报告指出，房屋局辖下独立审查组、屋宇署、消防处及劳工处，在监督宏福苑大维修工程涉及的火警风险方面均存在不同程度的不足及缺失。当局决定调查、厘清各级人员的职责、是否履行应有监管责任，以及相关失误应由谁承担等问题，目标在三个月内完成。 独立委员会报告揭示香港楼宇维修制度存在许多问题，并提出120项建议。李家超说，楼宇大维修涉及庞大金额，容易成为犯罪集团介入的目标，港府将从制度和法律层面加强监管。其中一项重点改革，是将楼宇维修工程围标行为刑事化。当局建议订立具阻吓力的刑事罚则，违法者最高可被判监禁10年及罚款1000万港元（163万新元）。 港府也计划成立“楼宇维修支援及服务局”，改善大维修工程的支援及监督制度。此外，房屋局将于11月成立“公营房屋楼宇管制组”，取代现有的独立审查组，藉此重整公营房屋工程监管架构，堵塞制度漏洞。 被问到为何只有一名局长辞职，以及特首是否也要问责时，李家超多次重申已综合多方面考虑。他说：“在自我检讨的过程中，我考虑到政府需要推行大量改革，未来也有大量工作要落实。作为政府第一责任人，其中一项最重要的责任，是要带领政府直视问题、解决问题、落实未来的大量工作。” 中国国务院港澳办发表评论文章，指港府公布宏福苑火灾报告、问责事宜及改革措施，充分体现责任担当，有利香港加快实现由治及兴。 香港中文大学政务与政策科学学院讲师孔永乐接受《联合早报》访问时说，何永贤请辞展现了政治问责的精神。在行政问责层面，港府已启动部门首长责任制下的两级调查机制，并转介公务员叙用委员会，预计三个月内完成，相信港人均关注是否会有更多相关人员被追究责任。 他认为，宏福苑大火显露出港府系统的结构性问题，“虽然政府在调查报告出台前已提出多项改善措施，但关键仍在于违规人员会否受到应有的重罚。从行政管理角度而言，制度规范设计得再严密完美，但只有具威慑力的惩处案例，才能对体系产生真正的警示作用。这一点仍有待时间检验。”

item.title: 欧洲央行维持利率不变 拉加德淡化通胀扩散风险
item.description: 欧洲央行行长克里斯蒂娜·拉加德淡化了通胀从能源领域向其他领域扩散的风险。此前，她将提前卸任的消息盖过了周四欧洲央行维持利率不变这一决定的关注度。 拉加德试图让新闻发布会聚焦于货币政策，并透露她与其他决策者讨论过加息的可能性，但最终否决了这一想法。背后的原因是，目前缺乏证据表明能源价格飙升正在引发过度的工资上涨诉求或推动通胀预期显著上升。 不过，鉴于投资者倾向于预计欧洲央行12月将把存款利率再上调25个基点，拉加德仍为进一步收紧政策留出了空间，称欧洲央行走向“明确”。 拉加德周四在法兰克福对记者表示，“我们正在密切关注。目前，我们没有看到除预测中已经包含的因素之外还存在第二轮效应的风险。眼下，我们没有看到明显的第二轮效应风险。” 市场对欧洲央行12月加息的押注略有升温，定价显示届时加息幅度达到22个基点，相当于加息概率为88%，高于周四利率决定公布前的80%。 “欧洲央行10月维持利率不变，尽管近期大宗商品价格上涨，但其声明释放出明显的鸽派信号。我们认为，欧洲央行管理委员会正在为结束本轮紧缩周期铺路，不过欧洲央行仍为12月再次加息保留了可能性。” 拉加德提前离任的消息加剧了市场对能源成本和法国局势的担忧，并引发了继任之争。西班牙和荷兰的前央行行长成为接替她、执掌欧元区货币政策的竞争人选。 在借贷成本方面，欧洲央行目前按兵不动。自伊朗战争冲击能源市场以来，该行已经两次加息。本周欧洲央行与美联储均维持利率不变，预计日本央行周五也将采取同样行动。 外界普遍预计，欧洲央行决策者将在12月再次加息，届时更新的经济预测将显示通胀压力有多严重。全球债券收益率上升正在抑制需求，而困扰法国的市场、财政和政治紧张局势进一步加剧了全球债券收益率的升势。 “尽管能源冲击的全面影响仍在逐步显现，但迄今为止，基础通胀总体保持稳定，现阶段工资也没有出现明显反应，”欧洲央行在声明中表示。“自管理委员会上次会议以来，融资条件已经收紧，这可能会对通胀和经济增长构成下行压力。” 拉加德也特别关注核心价格的上涨。核心价格剔除了能源和食品等价格波动较大的项目。她表示，“在我们制定货币政策决定所采用的三方面评估框架中，基础通胀可能会占据尤为重要的位置。” 近期能源价格上涨推动9月份整体消费者价格指数上升3.8%，通胀预期也有所上升。自欧洲央行上次议息以来，油价已上涨逾6%，天然气价格则升至近四年来最高水平。 欧元区经济可能已经开始感受到压力：企业活动势头和信心均在减弱。欧盟统计局周五公布数据前，彭博对分析师的调查显示，第三季度经济增速可能放缓至0.2%。 拉加德表示，“最新数据表明，欧元区经济第三季度继续扩张。”她同时称，经济前景面临的风险偏向下行。“与此同时，能源价格再度上涨打击了消费者信心，融资成本上升也可能对经济构成压力。” .appendQr_wrap{border:1px solid #E6E6E6;padding:8px;} .appendQr_normal{float:left;} .appendQr_normal img{width:100px;} .appendQr_normal_txt{float:left;font-size:20px;line-height:100px;padding-left:20px;color:#333;} 责任编辑：江学思

item.title: 焦点 | 欧洲经济风光不再 高福利还能撑多久？
item.description: 欧洲多国接连爆发示威。民众都不满生活费高涨、工资增长缓慢，以及公共服务承受压力等问题，愤怒都指向经济困境。欧洲曾经凭借强大的工业实力，称霸全球。但如今，传统产业优势受到挑战，在科技创新领域，也面对美国和中国的激烈竞争。欧盟委员会预测，欧元区今年经济增长只有0.9%，比2016年的1.8%低了一半。欧洲经济为何失去增长动力？改革又为什么如此困难？欧洲传统工业优势受到挑战欧洲汽车工业曾经在全球市场占据重要地位。2000年，欧盟生产的汽车占全球总产量约30%，到了2022年，比重已经下降至15%。
